what: Keep a help message that could not be sent and send it by itself when the internet is back, instead of "Couldn't send. Try again"
why: A member in a gym basement with weak signal must remember to come back and press Send again; many never will, and the team never hears the problem.
impact_why: Gym floors often have poor signal, which is exactly where members hit problems
my_view: My view: do it; show it in "Your questions" as "Waiting to send" so the member sees it was kept.

what: Let the floating feedback button add a picture of the screen it was opened from (member can remove it before Send)
why: The message carries the screen's name but no picture, so the team often has to ask what the member saw; a screenshot settles most reports in one look.
impact_why: Cuts back-and-forth on every bug report during the early-days period when the button is on for everyone
my_view: My view: worth doing; off by default with a clear "Add a picture of this screen" tick, so nothing private goes without a choice, and the privacy notice says so.

what: When a member taps "No" on "Did this solve it?", offer "Tell me when the team answers" and ask for notification permission right there
why: The team's answer pops up only on Android and only when notifications were already allowed; otherwise the member must remember to reopen Help to find it.
impact_why: A reply nobody reads is support work wasted, and an unanswered member is likely to leave
my_view: My view: do it; asking at the moment the member wants an answer is when people say yes.

what: If the coach comes back, write its suggested-weight reasons in the member's own unit (kg or lb)
why: The coach's reasons are written with kg in the words ("start with the empty bar (20 kg)", "starting light at 7.5 kg"), so a pound user would read kg inside the coach.
impact_why: Only matters once the hidden coach is shown again, and only for pound users
my_view: My view: park it with the coach; fix it in the same change that turns the coach back on.

what: Ask for a Play Store rating inside the app (Google's own in-app review card) at a happy moment: a new personal best or the 10th finished workout, at most once in a few months
why: The phone app has no in-app rating ask anywhere in its Android parts, so the Play listing gets ratings only from members who go looking; the happy moments are already known to the app
impact_why: Ratings and their count drive Play search rank and the install rate of every gym's invite link; this is the cheapest lever on store conversion
my_view: My view: do it. One small native call, shown after a PR or a milestone, never after a failed save. The store listing text itself belongs to the store area; this is only the ask.

what: Make the rest timer an Android 16 "Live Update": the countdown shows as a chip in the status bar and at the top of the lock screen, not only inside the notification list
why: Today the rest card is an ordinary notification with a drawn countdown; on Android 16 Google promotes timers like this to a status bar chip, which Google Clock already uses (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Rest is the most-seen moment of every workout; seeing seconds left without pulling down the shade saves a swipe each set
my_view: My view: worth it, keep the current card for older phones. Test on his phone first; what the watch copies must not change.

what: Add a third app-icon shortcut "Check in" that opens the gym poster scanner, for members who have joined a gym
why: The long-press menu holds only Start (or Resume) and Log body weight, though up to four fit; checking in today means open app, Gym tab, scan, and only the "Gym right now" widget skips that, which few members add
impact_why: Every gym visit starts with a check-in; one long-press instead of three taps at the gym door
my_view: My view: do it. The scanner link already exists for the widget; show it only to members in a gym.

what: Let the "Time to train" reminder say what to beat today ("Push 1 · try Bench 62.5 kg x 8"), the same line the Today widget already shows
why: The reminder only says "Next: Push 1" or "Open MettleUp to start your workout", easy to swipe away; a concrete target is a reason to go
impact_why: Reminders are the one push every opted-in member gets on training days; a specific target lifts the tap rate
my_view: My view: do it. Reuse the widget's what-to-beat line word for word (never a new guess); keep the plain line when there is no last time.

what: When Plus is switched on, let the app show a free trial set up in Play (for example 7 days) instead of only the base price
why: The pay code picks only the plain base plan and skips every Play offer, so a free trial or launch discount set up in Play would never reach the member
impact_why: A free trial is the usual way fitness apps such as Strong and Hevy turn free members into payers (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live); behind a switch today, so no member is affected yet
my_view: My view: decide before Plus goes live; a small change once he picks a trial length. Money wording must pass member-words first.

what: On the Today widget, when there is no plan or the plan day has no exercises, make the button "Start" (an empty workout) instead of "Open"
why: A member with no plan sees "No plan yet / Open MettleUp to start a workout" and must open the app, find the Workout tab and press Start; the widget could start it in one tap
impact_why: Saves two taps for members who train without a plan, a common way to begin
my_view: My view: do it with the same one-time key the Start button already uses, so no other app can start a workout.

what: Send each lift's sets and reps to Health Connect with the workout, not only "Strength training" with a start, end and calories
why: Google Health and Samsung Health show a MettleUp workout as a bare block; Health Connect can hold the exercise parts and reps, so members who live in those apps see what they trained
impact_why: Matters to members who use Samsung Health or Fitbit as their main record
my_view: My view: later. Nice for trust, but each lift must map to Health Connect's fixed exercise list; do it only if members ask.

what: Offer "Add <gym> to your home screen" once more at a good moment (the first real check-in at the gym), not only once after joining
why: The gym logo shortcut is the gym's own icon on the member's phone, the most visible piece of gym branding; it is asked for in one place and never again
impact_why: A gym icon on the home screen keeps the gym, and the app, in daily sight; owners pay for that branding
my_view: My view: do it, once per member, after the first check-in; never more than twice in total.

what: On "We did not find your number at a gym on MettleUp", add the "Recommend MettleUp to my gym" button
why: This card already says "Your gym may not use MettleUp yet", the exact moment a member is most willing to nudge their gym, but it only offers Set up the app or Try another number. The recommend button lives on the third intro screen and the Gym tab, which this member has already passed.
impact_why: Every member whose gym is not on MettleUp lands here; it is the cheapest owner lead source we have
my_view: My view: do it; one extra button that reuses the share message the Gym tab already sends, no new words to approve beyond the button.

what: Let the member type their gym's name (optional) before the recommend message goes out, and carry it in the shared link
why: The recommend link only says ?from=member, so a lead in HQ shows that a member shared it but not which gym. Sales cannot tell which gym to call when the owner does not reply.
impact_why: Turns an anonymous share into a gym name the sales team can follow up
my_view: My view: worth it with the button above; gym name only, never the member's name or number, so nothing new to promise in privacy.

what: On the not-found card, add "Have a gym code or poster? Join my gym" so the member does not go Back, Try another way, Join my gym
why: A member whose gym is on MettleUp but has another number for them is told to tap Back, then Try another way, then Join my gym. That is three taps and a screen they have to find; the card could open the code and poster view directly.
impact_why: Saves three taps for members on the right gym with an old number on file
my_view: My view: do it; the Join my gym view already exists, this is one more link on the card.

what: On the not-found card, also say the first name must be spelled the way the gym has it
why: The search needs both the number and the first name ("as your gym has it"). A member typed as "Priya" at the desk who types "Priyanka" is told only that the gym may have another number, so they try numbers, not names.
impact_why: A wrong-spelling miss today sends a real gym member into the no-gym setup
my_view: My view: do it as a words change (member-words skill); a second try with the right name costs nothing but a fresh WhatsApp check.

what: Drop the separate kg or lb step: preselect kg (the phone sign-in already assumes kg for Indian numbers) and show the choice on step 1 or 3
why: Setup is three steps and one of them is a single question most Indian members answer the same way. Picking kg does not move on by itself, so it is two taps for one answer. Hevy and Strong (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live) default units from the phone's region and let you change them later.
impact_why: Every member who sets up without a gym pays this step
my_view: My view: do it; setup becomes 2 steps, and the lb member still sees the choice with kg already ticked.

what: On the "We set you up as New to lifting" note, ask the experience question right there (three choices) instead of only pointing to Profile
why: A member who goes straight into the gym never answers setup, so a lifter of five years is set as "New to lifting". That changes rep ranges for strength goals, muscle tips and suggested plans. The note sends them to Profile, which a separate finding says opens the wrong place.
impact_why: Every straight-in gym member, the main way in, starts on beginner advice unless they find Profile
my_view: My view: do it; one tap answers it on the card they already see, and fixes most of what the Open Profile link was for.

what: Remove the optional mobile number box from setup step 1
why: The box says it is "only for your gym, once you link one". With phone sign-in as the main way in, a member with a gym is found by number anyway, and a member without one has no use for it. It is an extra field, a check to fail (a foreign-number finding exists) and a personal detail we keep for nothing.
impact_why: Fewer fields on the first screen, and less personal data kept
my_view: My view: remove it from setup and keep it in Profile only; check first that the gym link does not read it after a code join.

what: Move "Load demo data instead" off the member welcome into a hidden spot for sales demos
why: Demo data is for showing MettleUp off, yet every member who opens Try another way sees it. It can replace their own records (a separate S1 finding), and a real member who taps it ends up in a sample account called Arjun.
impact_why: Removes a trap for real members; sales and tests can still reach it
my_view: My view: do it with the S1 fix; keep it behind a long-press on the logo or a link, since the phone tests use it as their way in.

what: Add "From FitNotes" (and a plain spreadsheet file) to Bring your workouts
why: Bring workouts offers only Hevy and Strong. FitNotes is a long-standing free Android logger used by many Indian gym-goers (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live), and many members keep a notebook or spreadsheet. A member who cannot bring their history has less reason to switch.
impact_why: Helps a smaller group of switchers keep their history
my_view: My view: later, only if members ask for it in feedback; the Hevy and Strong readers are the pattern to copy.

what: On the exercise page, add "Add to a routine" and "Start a workout with this" to its menu
why: The exercise page shows history and how-to, but its menu only edits, hides, merges or resets records; a member who reads about an exercise and wants to do it must leave, open a routine, find the exercise again and add it
impact_why: Removes three or four taps from the most natural moment to plan a session
my_view: My view: do it, Add to a routine first (pick the routine from a short list); "Start a workout with this" second, only if no workout is open.

what: Let a member tap a record on the Records page and share it as a picture (lift, weight and reps, date, the gym logo for gym members)
why: Today only a whole month can be shared, from an icon on Profile; a new best is the moment members most want to show off, and every shared picture with the gym logo is free advertising for the gym. Hevy and Strong (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live) put records on their shared workout pictures
impact_why: A growth loop that costs nothing per share and helps the gym owner, who pays
my_view: My view: do it with the month picture's design; show the lift only, never body weight or anything a stranger could divide back into body weight.

what: Make a tap on a photo in the Body page's photo strip open that photo, not the list of all photos
why: Every photo in the strip goes to the full photos page, so the member taps once more to find the one they tapped
impact_why: One tap saved on a page members open weekly
my_view: My view: do it; open the full-screen viewer on that photo, with the list behind it for Back.

what: When taking a progress photo, show the last photo faintly over the camera so the member stands in the same spot and pose
why: The add sheet says "Same spot, same light, every few weeks", but nothing helps the member match it, so before-and-after pictures often compare different angles and distances
impact_why: Better before-and-after pictures keep members going and are what they share
my_view: My view: worth doing, but after the record sharing; it needs a camera screen of our own instead of the phone's camera.

what: Let a member set a goal body weight and draw it as a line on the body weight graph, with "x kg to go"
why: Many Indian gym members join to lose or gain weight, but the Body page only draws past weigh-ins; there is no goal to measure them against, so the graph never says how close they are
impact_why: Weight is the reason most members join; a visible goal brings them back to weigh in
my_view: My view: do it, optional and private (never shown to gym mates or on share pictures); one number in Edit profile next to the goal they already pick.

what: Offer one opt-in reminder: "Time for your weigh-in and progress photo" (weekly weigh-in, photo every 4 weeks)
why: The app reminds members about workouts but nothing reminds them to weigh in or take a photo, so the Body page goes stale after the first week and the before-and-after never happens
impact_why: Regular body entries are what make day-30 progress visible
my_view: My view: do it as off by default, offered once after the second weigh-in; one quiet notice, never a nag.

what: Add "Ask my trainer to measure me" on the Body page for gym members, sent to the gym's help inbox
why: The Body page already shows measurements the gym's trainer took, but a member has no way to ask for a check; trainers only measure members who remember to ask at the desk
impact_why: A trainer touch every month is what keeps members renewing, which is what the owner pays for
my_view: My view: worth doing once the help inbox is proven with gyms; no booking, just a message the trainer sees.

what: Keep the 1-rep max and plate calculators free; keep suggested weight and reps in MettleUp Plus
why: A free member who taps the calculator is sent to the Plus page. Free calculators are one search away on the web, so this lock earns little and makes the app feel stingy at a moment of effort
impact_why: Small money at stake either way; the gain is goodwill and fewer dead ends
my_view: My view: lift the lock, but it is your pricing call; if you keep it, show the result blurred with "Plus shows this" instead of jumping to the Plus page.

what: Decide on the switched-off Quick workout and "Muscles ready today": bring them back or delete them
why: You switched both off on 5 Nov 2026 but their screens stay in every build with nothing opening them, so they still have to be kept working through every change
impact_why: Less code to keep working and test; no member sees a change
my_view: My view: delete them unless you plan to bring them back within two releases; the code stays in history if you change your mind.

what: On the workout summary, give "Summary unavailable" a Try again button
why: When the summary cannot be read after Finish, the member gets only Done; every other page in this area (a saved workout, a routine, records, photos, the report) already offers Try again, so this is the one dead end at the proudest moment of the day
impact_why: Rare, but it hits right after a finished workout, when the member most wants to see the result
my_view: My view: do it; the same Try again the other pages use, re-reading the summary. The workout is already saved, so this is only about not losing the payoff screen.

what: For a gym member, add the gym's Bring a friend link to a shared workout picture and text (one line: "Train with me at <gym>")
why: Sharing a workout is the moment a member is proudest, and the picture already carries the gym's brand; today a friend who sees it has no way to act, while the Bring a friend link (the enquiry lands with the gym) lives only on the Gym tab
impact_why: Turns every shared workout into a possible new paying gym member, which is what gym owners pay MettleUp for
my_view: My view: do it once Bring a friend is live on the server; add the link to the text share and a small "Join me at <gym>" line on the picture, with a switch to leave it off. Never for a member with no gym.

what: For a member with no gym, end the share text and the picture footer with where to get the app ("Logged with MettleUp, mettleup.fit")
why: The picture says only "Logged with MettleUp" and the text share carries no app name or link, so a friend who likes it cannot find the app; Hevy and Strong share cards carry the app name as a watermark (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Free installs from every share, at no cost; small but it adds up
my_view: My view: do it, short web address only (no long Play link on the picture). Keep the text share clean for pasting into an AI chat: one last line, nothing more.

what: Ask for a Google Play rating at a good moment: after a workout that beat last time, from about the 5th workout, at most once in a few months
why: The app never asks for a rating anywhere; the Finish screen already knows when a member beat last time or hit a milestone, which is the best moment to ask. Ratings drive store conversion
evidence: data:grep requestReview|StoreReview|rate us over apps/mobile/src = 0 hits
impact_why: More and better stars lift the Play listing for every new member and gym owner who checks it
my_view: My view: do it with Google's own in-app review sheet (Google decides whether to show it; the member never leaves the app). Never after a lighter-day workout or a failed save.

what: Show "about 50 min" on the routine preview and on Up next, from how long this routine took the last few times
why: Members plan around time ("do I have time before work?"); the preview shows only the day type, exercise count and folder. Fitbod lets members pick a workout length and shows it (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Seen before every workout; helps busy members start instead of skipping
my_view: My view: do it from past workouts of the same routine only; show nothing for a routine never done (no guessing).

what: On Up next, for a gym member, add one line "Gym open till 10 pm" or "Gym closed today" that opens Gym timings
why: Gym timings are two taps away on the Gym tab; the moment a member decides to go is on Up next. The gym already keeps its hours and special days in MettleUp
impact_why: Saves a wasted trip on a holiday or a special closing day
my_view: My view: worth it, but only the line, no new screen; hide it when the hours cannot be read rather than guessing.

what: In Find a plan, add a "From your gym" section listing the plans the gym's trainer sent
why: Find a plan shows Build a plan, ready programs and importing, but not the trainer's plans, which arrive as folders on the Workout tab; a member looking for a plan here misses the one their own gym made
impact_why: Makes the trainer's work visible where members look for plans, which is value the owner pays for
my_view: My view: do it, only when the gym has trainer plans switched on; each row opens the existing folder, no copy.

what: On the monthly report and year in review, add a clear "Share my month" button at the bottom, beside the text share
why: Sharing the picture is only a small paper-plane icon in the top bar, while the text share has a full row at the bottom. The report is the most shareable page; Strava's year in review is built around sharing (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: More shares of the report means more people seeing MettleUp and the gym
my_view: My view: do it; keep the top icon too. Pairs with telling the member the report is ready (already proposed).

what: Offer an optional "photo day" reminder every 4 weeks on the Progress photos page, off until the member turns it on
why: The page already tells members to take a photo "every few weeks" but nothing reminds them; progress photos show change that the weight on the bar does not, and members forget them
impact_why: Keeps members who train for looks coming back and seeing change, which helps day-30 retention
my_view: My view: worth trying, opt-in only, using the same reminder system as workout reminders.

what: Let a member add a screenshot to Help and feedback
why: Help and feedback takes typed or spoken words and the watch log, but not a picture; most app problems are easier to show than describe, and the team answers faster with one
impact_why: Fewer back-and-forth replies on bug reports
my_view: My view: later, not now; worth it once feedback volume grows. It must warn that a screenshot can show personal numbers, and it needs server storage.

what: Put a small "+ Add" on each shop card for a product with one size or flavour, so a member adds a protein bar or water from the grid without opening the product page
why: Today every add costs a trip: tap the card, the product page opens, tap Add to bag, then go back; members buying the same small item every visit pay that each time
impact_why: Cuts two taps on the most common shop buy; the bag badge already shows the count
my_view: My view: do it, only for one-option products in stock; products with sizes or flavours keep the page so nobody orders the wrong one.

what: Add "Order again" on a collected or cancelled order in My orders: it puts the same items back in the bag at today's prices
why: Regulars reorder the same shake or supplement; My orders only shows status, pay and cancel, so a repeat buy means finding each product again
impact_why: Repeat buys are most shop orders at a gym counter; one tap instead of a search
my_view: My view: do it. Re-price from the live list and say plainly when an item is gone or out of stock, as the bag already does.

what: On an out-of-stock product, offer "Tell me when it is back" (one pop-up when the gym restocks it), and show the owner how many members are waiting for it
why: The product page shows a dead "Out of stock" button and nothing else, so the sale is lost and the owner never learns the demand
impact_why: Turns a lost sale into an order and gives the owner a restock signal
my_view: My view: worth it once the shop has real use; it needs one small server list and one pop-up, so wait until the shop switch is on for paying gyms.

what: Make the "Check in" row on My gym show today's answer ("Checked in today at 6:42 pm" or "Not checked in today"), and add "12th visit this month" to the check-in done screen
why: The row always says the same "Scan the gym's check-in QR" line, so a member cannot tell if today counted; the month's visit count already reaches the phone but shows only inside My membership
impact_why: Check-in is the daily habit of every joined member; seeing it count is the cheapest motivation and cuts "did it work?" questions at the desk
my_view: My view: do it; both numbers already reach the phone. Count visits, not streaks, so a rest day never feels like failure.

what: Ask for a friend at the happy moment: on the "You're checked in" screen (and after a new personal best), show the Bring a friend invite with a direct WhatsApp button, not only the card at the bottom of My gym
why: Today the invite is the last card on My gym and opens the general share menu; a member standing in the gym right after a check-in is the most likely to bring a training partner. Cult.fit and most fitness apps ask at a finished-session moment (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Referral is the gym's cheapest new member, and every friend who joins is also a new MettleUp phone
my_view: My view: do it, at most once a month per member, and never on the "already checked in" repeat screen.

what: Show what Bring a friend has earned: "2 friends joined, 14 free days added" instead of only "Friends who joined: 0"
why: A bare "Friends who joined: 0" reads as a failure and never shows the reward landing; the reward days per friend are already on the phone
impact_why: A visible reward is what makes referral programmes repeat
my_view: My view: do it, and hide the count line while it is 0 so a new member sees the offer, not a zero.

what: Let a member add one photo to a complaint or feedback in Message your gym (a broken machine, a leaking tap, a dirty washroom)
why: Gym complaints are mostly about things; words alone make the desk walk around to find them. Trainerize and the Mindbody branded apps take photos in messages (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Faster fixes for the owner and a member who feels heard; also a better record if a complaint is checked later
my_view: My view: worth doing after the storage caps are settled (pictures small, deleted after 90 days); not before.

what: On the leaderboard, give a member outside the top 10 one line of reach: "3 more workouts to pass #10" (Workouts tab only)
why: A member at rank 23 sees the top 10 and their own row, with no next step; a near goal is what keeps people coming back
impact_why: Gives the middle of the pack, the biggest group, a reason to come in this week
my_view: My view: do it for the Workouts count only; on kg lifted a gap number can be worked back into a body weight, so leave that tab as it is.

what: Add "Remind me" next to "Quietest later today: 2 pm to 4 pm" on the How busy card: one phone reminder at the start of that window
why: The card already works out the quiet window but the member has to remember it; the reminder system that could carry it already exists
impact_why: Nice for members who dislike crowds; small reach while the busy card waits for enough check-ins
my_view: My view: later. Only once the busy card is live for real gyms; until then it is a button on a hidden card.

what: Offer "Pay now by UPI" on the bag itself, next to Place order, when the gym takes online payments, so paying is part of placing the order
why: Today the bag always says pay at the desk; paying online means placing the order, landing on My orders and finding the pay buttons there
impact_why: Shorter desk queues and fewer unpaid ready orders for the owner
my_view: My view: do it after the paid-order wording faults are fixed, so the order and the bag tell the same story.

what: Do not build class or slot booking yet; first ask 5 paying owners whether their members book anything
why: Mindbody, PushPress and Cult.fit centre their member apps on booking classes (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live); the Gym tab has none and its "what a gym gives you" list leaves it out on purpose
impact_why: Indian open-floor gyms rarely run booked classes; building it now costs months for a few studios
my_view: My view: do not build now. Revisit only if owners ask, and then start with a fixed weekly timetable members can read, not bookings.

what: Make the "Your plan ends on Friday" card on the Workout tab, and the plan-ending reminders, open the Renew my plan list straight away when the gym offers plans in the app
why: Today both open the Gym tab in general and the member has to find My membership and tap Renew my plan. The piece that opens the renew list directly is already written but nothing uses it any more
impact_why: Renewals are the gym owner's money; every member gets this card once a plan cycle
my_view: My view: do it; two taps fewer at the exact moment a member is ready to renew. Keep "Renew at the front desk" only for gyms with no plans in the app (the wording fault is already a finding).

what: Put an "Ask about this" button under the gym's Offer and Event messages that opens Message your gym with that message quoted
why: Gym messages are read-only today: a member who wants the Diwali PT offer has to remember it, go to Message your gym and type it out, or walk to the desk
impact_why: Turns the owner's broadcast into a reply he can sell to; Mindbody and Glofox member apps tie offers to a booking or buy button (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
my_view: My view: do it; it reuses the existing message thread, so no new server work beyond a quoted first line.

what: Add "Order again" on a collected shop order, which fills the bag with the same items in one tap
why: Members buy the same protein shake or water bottle again and again; today they browse and pick each item again
impact_why: Repeat buys are most of a gym counter's sales; Swiggy, Zomato and Blinkit all lead with reorder (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
my_view: My view: do it; the bag and the stock check already exist, so this only copies the lines of an old order into the bag.

what: After a QR check-in, offer "Start today's gym workout" when the gym posted a workout of the day, next to the member's own routine
why: The check-in screen offers only the member's own routine; the gym's workout of the day sits on the Workout tab and many members never see it at the moment they arrive
impact_why: The trainer's daily work gets used; check-in is the one moment every gym member is in front of the app
my_view: My view: do it; show it as the second button so the member's own plan stays first.

what: When a member finishes the gym's monthly challenge, offer a share picture ("I finished the November challenge at <gym>") that carries their bring-a-friend invite link
why: Bring a friend only lives on its own card; the proud moment after a challenge is when people share, and the share would carry the gym's free days to a friend
impact_why: A new member for the gym and a new app user for us, from a share that costs nothing; Strava and cult.fit lean on share cards (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
my_view: My view: do it after the challenge card is shown in a phone test; put only the goal reached on the picture, never kg lifted or rank numbers that can give away private data.

what: Give a member a reward (for example 3 months of MettleUp Plus) when the gym they recommended signs up, by putting a member code in the Recommend MettleUp to my gym link
why: The recommend link only says "from a member"; the member never hears back and has no reason to push the owner twice
impact_why: Members are the cheapest route into new gyms; a reward and a "your gym joined" note turn one share into a follow-up
my_view: My view: worth it once Plus is switched on; until then just add the code so HQ can thank the member by hand. Pairs with letting the member type the gym's name.

what: Let a Complaint to the gym carry one photo (a broken machine, a dirty washroom)
why: A typed complaint about "the second treadmill" is hard to act on; the desk then has to find the member to ask
impact_why: Helps owners fix things faster, but complaints are a small share of messages
my_view: My view: wait; first put a size cap on what members store in the shared database (already a finding for workout reports), then allow one small photo on complaints only.

what: Once every gym server has the newest trainer-share function, drop the two older ways the phone still tries when sharing workouts with trainers
why: The phone keeps three versions of the same send and falls back through them, which is what lets an older server get a different amount of history
impact_why: No member sees it; it cuts code that can send the wrong amount of history
my_view: My view: do it after checking the server has the newest version live; one less place for the privacy wording to drift from what is sent.

what: Add a 5-second "Get ready" count before a plank or hold countdown starts, so the member can put the phone down and get into position
why: Start begins the countdown at once; a plank is done with the phone on the floor, so the first seconds of every hold go on getting down
impact_why: Every timed set (planks, wall sits, holds) loses a few seconds and the saved time is wrong by that much
my_view: My view: do it; a short lead-in with a beep is how interval and plank timers work, and it makes the saved time honest.

what: At zero on a hold countdown, keep counting past the goal ("+0:07") until the member taps Stop, instead of saving exactly the goal time
why: The set saves itself at the goal, so a member who holds longer can never record more than the goal and never sees progress on holds
impact_why: Holds can only go up when the member retypes the time by hand
my_view: My view: do it with the bell at zero still ringing; if the member does not touch the phone for 10 seconds after zero, save the goal time as today.

what: Open the plate calculator from the barbell set itself (a small "20 + 10 each side" line under the open set, or a long press on the weight), not only from the exercise menu
why: Today it takes the three-dot menu, then Plate calculator, then checking the weight, in the middle of loading the bar
impact_why: Asked at every barbell set by newer lifters; fewer taps between sets
my_view: My view: do the one grey line under the open barbell set first; it answers the question without opening anything. Keep it free if the owner agrees with the earlier "calculators free" idea.

what: Offer the plate calculator for plate-loaded machines too (leg press, hack squat, T-bar row), counting plates per side with no bar
why: The plate calculator shows only for barbell exercises, yet the leg press and hack squat are loaded with the same plates
impact_why: Helps on leg day; the maths is the same minus the bar
my_view: My view: worth it after the barbell line above; it needs a "plate-loaded" mark on those library machines, which is the real work.

what: On Finish workout, add a one-tap "How did it feel?" (for example Easy, Good, Hard) above the typed note
why: The only way to record how a workout went is typing in a note box, which few members do on a phone after training
impact_why: Gives the member and a trainer a simple history of hard days, and a signal for when to suggest an easy week
my_view: My view: do it, optional and one tap; show it in history. Do not feed it into the suggested weights until members are seen using it.

what: Put a small QR code on the "IN USE" sign with "Get MettleUp free" (for a gym member: the gym’s own join or Bring a friend link)
why: The owner put the logo on the sign because people look at the phone and ask which app; a code turns that look into an install without the member stopping to explain
impact_why: The sign is shown to other gym-goers many times a day by every member who uses it
my_view: My view: do it, small and below the clock so the sign still reads from metres away; it needs a QR drawing library added to the app, so check its size first.

what: On the "Make your first routine" card, add a second choice "Or pick a ready plan" that opens Find a plan
why: A new member with no routines is offered only making one by hand; the ready programs (gym, dumbbells, home, beginner to advanced) sit behind a different button
impact_why: Most beginners do not know which exercises to pick; a ready plan gets them to the first workout faster
my_view: My view: do it; one text link under the main button, no new screen.

what: Let a member set a goal for one lift ("Bench press 100 kg") and draw it as a line on that exercise’s chart, with "7.5 kg to go"
why: The exercise chart shows the past only; members train towards a number but the app never holds it for them
impact_why: A clear target per lift keeps members coming back to see the gap close
my_view: My view: worth building after the body-weight goal idea, using the same goal-line drawing; a few goals at most, no reminders at first.

what: Offer the how-to steps of library exercises in Hindi (a switch on the demo sheet), using the same short steps
why: Search already understands Hindi and Hinglish gym words, but the steps that teach the movement are English only, and many members read English as a second language
impact_why: Helps beginners do the movement right; reach in smaller-city gyms
my_view: My view: not yet; ask 5 members of a paying gym first whether English steps stop them, then translate the 50 most-used exercises before the whole library.

what: Under each routine on the Workout tab, add when it was last done ("Last done Tue" or "Not done yet") next to the exercise list
why: A member choosing between Push, Pull and Legs has to remember which one they did last; the card only lists exercise names. Strong shows "last performed" on each template (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live).
impact_why: Seen every time a member picks a routine by hand instead of Up next
my_view: My view: do it; one short grey line from the workout history the app already keeps. Keep the exercise list as the second line.

what: Give the Progress tab's "Today" card its own Start button, so the member starts today's workout from there
why: Today the card only opens the Workout tab, where the member taps Start again: one extra tap and a screen change at the moment they want to train.
impact_why: Saves one tap for members who open Progress first
my_view: My view: do it; reuse Up next's own start guard so the two Start buttons can never start two workouts.

what: Show "Watch your trainer" on the exercise's card during a live workout (a small video link), not only on the exercise's own page
why: The gym trainer's video is most useful mid-workout, at the machine; today it shows only on the exercise page, which the member must open from the card menu and come back from.
impact_why: Makes the gym's own content visible where members use it, which is the gym-owner selling point
my_view: My view: do it, small and only when the trainer gave a video; it makes the gym feel present inside the app.

what: After a member's first 2 weeks, offer a weekly goal on Up next with the number they actually trained ("You trained 3 times a week. Make 3 your goal?" Set / Not now)
why: The weekly goal is off for everyone and lives deep in Settings, so most members never see "This week: 2 of 3 workouts", the line that keeps people coming back.
impact_why: A weekly target is one of the strongest reasons members are still training on day 30
my_view: My view: do it; one card, asked once, with the goal already filled in from their own weeks; Not now hides it for good.

what: Let the workout share picture use one of that workout's own photos as its background
why: Members already add up to 4 photos to a workout, but the share picture is always a plain card; a gym selfie with the numbers on it is what people post to WhatsApp status and Instagram. Hevy lets members share a workout over their own photo (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live).
impact_why: More shared pictures carrying the MettleUp and gym name means more people asking which app it is
my_view: My view: worth building after the share-link ideas already listed; the before/after share already handles member photos, so reuse it. Say clearly that the photo leaves the phone only when they share.

what: On the Profile history chart, add one line comparing with the period before ("12% more kg than the 3 months before")
why: The chart shows a total and a line, but a member cannot tell at a glance whether they are doing more or less than before, which is the question the chart exists to answer.
impact_why: A clear "up" line is a small reward each time they open Profile
my_view: My view: do it, but only when the earlier period has workouts; never show a negative line in red, say "less than" calmly.

what: Keep a discarded workout for about 10 seconds with an Undo bar, instead of wiping it the moment 'Discard workout?' is confirmed
why: A mis-tap on the confirm loses a whole live workout for good; the saved copy is cleared in the same step
impact_why: Rare, but it costs the member an hour of logging and their trust in the app
my_view: My view: do it; the app already shows Undo bars for deleted sets and routine swaps, so it is the same pattern on one more button.

what: Offer Undo after deleting a routine or a whole folder (a folder takes every routine inside it with it)
why: Today a folder delete removes all its routines at once after one question, with no way back; a member who built a 4-day plan by hand loses all of it
impact_why: Routines are the member's own work; losing them is the kind of mistake that ends a habit
my_view: My view: do it for folders first (the bigger loss); routines can follow with the same snapshot-and-restore code.

what: Make the plan builder start from the member's last answers (days, split, minutes, equipment, sore spots), not from the defaults each time
why: Every start resets to 3 days, 60 minutes, gym equipment; only goal and level come from the profile, so a member rebuilding their plan after 8 weeks answers all 5 steps again
impact_why: Saves 4 or 5 taps on a screen used every few weeks
my_view: My view: do it; keep the answers on the phone with the rest of the workout settings, and still let the member change any step.

what: Remember the exercise picked under Progress, Your lifts, 'Any exercise' after the app restarts
why: The pick is kept in memory only; after a restart Progress jumps back to the most-trained lift, so a member following one lift (for example Deadlift) picks it again every time
impact_why: Small, but it is on the screen members open to see progress
my_view: My view: do it; one saved value, cleared if that exercise is merged or removed.

what: Let the gym set its plates and bars once in the panel, and give that setup to every member of the gym as the starting plate calculator setup
why: Today each member sets up the gym's plates and bars on their own phone; most never do, so the plate calculator assumes standard plates the gym may not have
impact_why: A small 'your gym knows its own kit' moment for every member, and a reason for the owner to open the panel
my_view: My view: worth doing after the busier gym features; the member's own change should still win over the gym's setup.

what: When a member joins or moves to a new gym, ask once: 'New gym, new machines? Start machine and cable records fresh from today' and apply it to those exercises in one go
why: 'Start records fresh' exists but only one exercise at a time, and only from today; its own notes name 'a new gym, a new machine' as the reason, yet a member moving gyms would have to do it on every machine exercise
impact_why: Machine weights differ between gyms; without this the new gym's first weeks show fake 'worse than before' numbers
my_view: My view: do it as a single optional question on the join screen; free weights (barbell, dumbbell) stay untouched.

what: Suggest duplicate exercises to merge: an own exercise whose name matches a library exercise or one of its other names, for example after an import from Hevy or Strong
why: Merging works, but the member has to find duplicates by hand; an import from another app is the moment most duplicates appear
impact_why: Duplicates split one lift's history and records in two, which makes the charts look flat
my_view: My view: do it as a quiet 'Possible duplicates' line on the Exercises list; never merge without the member's tap, since a merge cannot be undone.

what: When a member keeps changing the rest on one exercise to the same length (for example 3 workouts in a row skipping to 1:30 on curls), offer 'Make 1:30 the rest for curls?'
why: The per-exercise rest is only set by hand; members rarely find that setting, so the timer keeps ringing at the wrong time
impact_why: Fewer interruptions in every workout for members who never open the settings
my_view: My view: maybe later; useful, but behind the ideas above, and it must ask once, never change the rest by itself.

what: Pick the next exercise demo films by what members actually do: first every exercise in the beginner ready programs and the most-logged lifts, then the rest
why: Only 2 of the roughly 400 library exercises have a demo film today, so almost every member opens an exercise and sees no film; the film queue is one a day, so its order decides what members get first
impact_why: A new member on Full Body Basics would see a film on every exercise of their first weeks instead of on two side exercises
my_view: My view: do it; it changes only the order of the queue the film tool already works through, no app change. The beginner programs hold a few dozen distinct exercises, about a month of the one-a-day pipeline.

what: Give the "lose fat" goal its own shape: a 10-minute cardio finish (treadmill, cycle or skipping) at the end of each plan-builder workout, and one ready "Fat loss, 3 days" gym program
why: Fat loss is one of the four goals a member can pick, but the builder leaves all cardio out and treats fat loss like muscle, and no ready program is written for it; weight loss is a very common reason people join an Indian gym
impact_why: A large group of new members picks this goal and today gets the same plan as someone building muscle
my_view: My view: do it; treadmill and cycle logging already exists, so it is one extra slot on fat-loss plans plus one program of data. Keep the lifting the same; the cardio is the only change, and say so on the plan.

what: Add a "Classic 5-day split" ready program (chest, back, shoulders, arms, legs: one muscle group a day), and a 2-day full-body program for busy weeks
why: The ready programs are only 3, 4 or 6 days a week, while the plan builder already accepts 2 to 6 days; the one-muscle-a-day split is what many Indian gym trainers write on the board, and a member who trains that way finds nothing familiar in the list
impact_why: Members who already follow a 5-day split can follow it in the app with Target lines from day one instead of building every routine by hand
my_view: My view: do it; it is data only (the program shape and the test that checks every exercise already exist). Say in its summary that training each muscle twice a week suits most people better, so we meet members where they are without calling it the best split.

what: Let the plan builder ask one optional extra question, "Anything to focus on?" (legs and glutes, upper body, arms, none), and add one more exercise for that area to each workout
why: The builder asks goal, level, equipment, days, time and sore areas but never what the member most wants to change; a glutes and legs focus is a common ask from women members, and Fitbod lets members set muscle priorities (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Makes the built plan feel made for the member, which is the reason to use the builder instead of a ready program
my_view: My view: worth doing after the fat-loss shape; keep it to one answer and one extra slot so the time per workout still fits, with "none" as the default.

what: Put the member's goal, level, training days a week and equipment (home, dumbbells, full gym) at the top of the "Ask your own AI" text, and ask the AI to answer in Hindi when the app is in Hindi or Hinglish
why: The text gives the AI only exercises and sets, so its advice can tell a home trainer to use a cable machine or a fat-loss member to bulk; the question is always in English even when the member reads Hindi
impact_why: Better answers from the AI make the feature worth repeating, but few members use it today
my_view: My view: do it; none of these four facts can identify the member or divide back to body weight, so the privacy promise holds. Keep name, phone and weight out as now.

what: Celebrate a new strength level on the finish screen ("Bench press: now Intermediate"), the day a best lift moves the member up a level
why: The level sits quietly under the chart on each exercise page, so a member who moves up a level usually never notices; a level change is rare and real, the kind of moment that keeps people coming back
impact_why: A rare, earned milestone at the end of a workout gives the member a reason to share and to return
my_view: My view: do it; show the level word only (no body weight, no ratio), the same privacy rule as the exercise page, and at most one level line per workout.

what: Let a gym owner attach a real reward to a badge in the panel (for example "50 workouts: a free shaker at the desk"), show it on the member's locked badge, and list who earned it on the desk screen
why: Badges live only on the member's phone; the code already notes a gym prize as a later idea. Gyms judge MettleUp on members still training on day 30, and a prize at 10 or 50 workouts is a cheap reason for a member to keep logging and for the owner to keep paying
impact_why: Ties the free app to the gym's own retention, the number the owner pays for
my_view: My view: worth building once more gyms are live; it needs the server to know which badges a member earned, so start with the workout-count badges (10 and 50), which typing made-up weights cannot fake.

what: Warn the member before an easy week starts, on the Today card ("Next week is an easy week: half the sets"), and let them move it from there
why: The easy week is explained only once it has begun, behind the i on the Target line and the Today card; a member planning a hard week finds out at the gym
impact_why: Fewer members skip the easy week by surprise, and the plan feels planned
my_view: My view: do it if cheap; the next-easy-week rule already exists, so it is one line on the Today card in the last days of the week before.

what: In the first routine guide, when the member taps a ready name (Push Day, Leg Day, Full Body...), open step 3 with 5 common exercises for that day already ticked, so they untick instead of searching the whole library
why: Step 3 shows the full exercise list with nothing picked, even though the app already knows the day type from the name tapped on step 2. A new member, often typing in a second language, has to find and tap every exercise one by one
impact_why: Every new member who takes the guide; the first routine is the step before the first workout
my_view: My view: do it. The day type and the library muscles are already there; picking 5 starters per day type is a small list. Keep them untickable and say 'You can change these'.

what: When a member has no routines and has skipped the first routine guide, show a small Up next card ('No routine yet') with 'Pick a ready plan' and 'Make a routine', instead of no card at all
why: After Skip, the guide never comes back, and the Up next card shows nothing for a member with no routines. That member sees only Start empty workout, the hardest way in for a beginner
impact_why: Members who skip setup are the ones most likely to stop in week 1
my_view: My view: do it. One more card state using words and screens that already exist; no new data.

what: When this week's goal is reached, change 'This week: 4 of 4 workouts' to a done state ('Weekly goal met. 4 of 4') with a tick, and on the next workout say 'Bonus workout'
why: The goal line counts up but never marks the moment it is reached. Hevy and Strong both lean on streak and goal moments (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live); ours stays a plain counter
impact_why: Seen once a week by members who set a goal; small lift to week-to-week habit
my_view: My view: do it, but after the open fault that this line counts days while saying workouts is fixed, so the celebration is never wrong.

what: For gym members, mark on the Calendar the days they checked in at the gym but logged no workout, with 'Log it' that opens a past workout for that day
why: Today a day without a logged workout is blank and a tap does nothing. A member who trained but forgot to log loses that day from the calendar, streaks and reports, and the app already knows they were at the gym
impact_why: Forgotten logs are common; filling them keeps streaks and the monthly report true, which keeps members using the app
my_view: My view: worth it for gym members only. Use the check-ins the phone already reads, show a hollow dot, and never log anything by itself.

what: Let 'Share routine' and 'Share folder' send a link: a friend with MettleUp taps it and the routine is added; a friend without it lands on the Play Store and gets the routine after install
why: Sharing today sends plain text ending 'Made with MettleUp' with no link, or a JSON file only another member can import by hand. Hevy shares routines as a link that opens in the app (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live). Friends sharing a plan is a free install loop we are not using
impact_why: Gym friends swap plans on WhatsApp all the time; each share can become an install
my_view: My view: good idea, but later. It needs a small web page and app links; as a first step, add the store link to the plain-text share (S) and see if anyone taps it.

what: Add 'Share to Instagram Story' as a direct button on the share sheet, sending the Story-size or see-through picture straight into Instagram's story editor
why: The picture already has a Story size and a see-through background built for Instagram, but the member still goes through the phone's general share menu, picks Instagram, then Story. Hevy shares straight to Instagram Stories (its shareables page, as cited in our own code; not re-checked live)
impact_why: Story shares carry the gym's logo and our name to the member's followers; fewer taps means more shares
my_view: My view: do it after checking that Instagram's story share works from our app on Android (it needs a Facebook app id). Keep the normal share button beside it.

what: In the exercise picker's Recent list, add the last best set beside the date ('Last: 12 Oct, 60 kg x 8')
why: While adding an exercise mid-workout, the member sees only when they last did it, not what they lifted, so they open the exercise or guess the weight to load
impact_why: Saves a look-up on many exercise adds; small but frequent
my_view: My view: do it if the last set is already read with the date; otherwise leave it, since the Previous line shows it once the exercise is added.

what: After a member taps 'Try 40 kg' on the stuck-lift card, show one line on the next workout's card: 'Last time you stepped back to 40 kg. Back to 45 kg when this feels easy'
why: The step-back ask explains why to go lighter, but nothing tells the member the plan to climb back. A member who stepped back may feel they lost progress and stop
impact_why: Only members with a stuck lift; it protects trust in the targets
my_view: My view: try it, but only as words. The engine's targets stay as they are; this line just says where they lead.

what: Do not add exercise videos to the library for now; keep the start and end pictures and the 2 to 4 how-to steps
why: The library already carries how-to steps and pictures for each exercise. Videos would add size, cost and a licence question (the picture supplier issue is still open) for little gain in a gym where a trainer can show the move
impact_why: Saves building and hosting work that members have not asked for
my_view: My view: skip videos until members ask for them in feedback; first settle the picture licence fault.

what: On the very first workout's finish screen, show 'Next time, beat these' with the best set of each lift (for example 'Bench 40 kg x 10')
why: The first workout deliberately shows no records, so the screen most new members see has no reason to come back for workout 2
impact_why: Workout 2 is where most new members drop off; this gives them a target the moment they finish
my_view: My view: do it; the sets are already on screen, it only picks the best one per lift. Keeps the honest rule of no fake records.

what: On the finish screen, add the badge the member is closest to ('3 more workouts to your 25 workouts badge'), when no new badge was earned
why: Badge progress is only shown on the Badges page, which few members open; the finish screen only says when one was earned
impact_why: Seen after every workout, turns the badge shelf into a reason to train again this week
my_view: My view: do it; the progress words already exist, show only one line, and only when it is within reach (for example 80 percent done).

what: Give a followed plan an end: ready programs carry a length (for example 8 or 12 weeks), and at the end the member sees 'Plan done' with what got stronger and a choice: repeat it a little heavier, or pick the next plan
why: A followed plan's week number only counts up; nothing ever says the plan is finished or what to do next
impact_why: A clear finish line and a next step keep members past month 2-3, when program apps (Fitbod, JEFIT, as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live) push a new block
my_view: My view: worth it after the free-plan basics; start with the ready programs only, gym plans keep their trainer's own length.

what: Let a member who finished the gym's workout of the day post a result (time or top weight) to a 'Today at <gym>' board other members of the gym can see, opt-in
why: The workout of the day only goes one way: the gym posts it, the member starts it, and nothing comes back to the gym or to other members
impact_why: Box-gym apps (SugarWOD, Wodify, as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live) are built on this whiteboard; it makes the gym's feature visibly used and gives owners a reason to keep posting
my_view: My view: not yet; first check how many gyms post a workout of the day. If a few do it daily, this is the next step, opt-in and first name only.

what: After two weeks on a plan the gym's trainer sent, ask once 'How is this plan?' (Too easy, Just right, Too hard) and send the answer to that trainer
why: Gym plans arrive on the phone and update, but the member has no way to tell the trainer how it is going
impact_why: Gives trainers a reason to adjust plans and talk to members, which owners sell as personal attention
my_view: My view: do it after gym plans are switched on for real gyms; one question, one tap, shown in the trainer's member page.

what: Under 'Ask your own AI', let the member pick the question at the end of the text: get stronger, build muscle, fix a weak muscle, or plan my next 4 weeks
why: The copied text always ends with the same question, so a member with a different goal has to edit it by hand in the chat app
impact_why: Small, but makes the free AI answer fit the member, which is the point of the feature
my_view: My view: do it; four fixed choices, no typing, nothing new leaves the phone.

what: Remove the AI-written finish note (Groq, behind a switch) and keep the plain fact note
why: It needs the coach switch, a setting and a Groq key, so almost nobody sees it, and the fact note already says what happened
impact_why: Less to keep alive: Groq has already retired models without warning once (Oct 2026)
my_view: My view: remove it unless the coach comes back; one fewer paid call and one fewer thing that can fail quietly.

what: When a forgotten workout pauses itself, the next app open asks 'Did you finish at 7:42 pm?' with Save, Keep going and Discard, instead of only showing a paused workout
why: The pause is back-dated and silent; the member finds a paused workout later and has to work out what to do
impact_why: Saves a confused moment and stops half-saved workouts sitting open for days
my_view: My view: do it; the end time is already worked out, this only asks the question once.

what: On a member's 10th, 25th, 50th and 100th workout, offer a share picture of the milestone ('My 50th workout') with the gym's name or the app's name
why: The milestone line shows on the finish screen but has no share of its own, and the code notes these are the most-shared moments among lifters
impact_why: A free word-of-mouth moment that brings in friends and gyms at no cost
my_view: My view: do it, reusing the existing workout share picture with the milestone as its title; no body weight on it.
